text5520009668863520_444798865.text: As the first responder on scene, your team’s access to AEDs and high-quality CPR is vital. Arm your agency with emergency solutions from Stryker’s system of care.

text.text:
Stay ready with AEDs in police vehicles

Be prepared for sudden cardiac events, anywhere, anytime

In law enforcement, you know you can’t predict when an emergency strikes, but you can be prepared. Sudden cardiac arrest can happen to anyone, anywhere. And a victim’s chance of survival dramatically decreases for every minute without treatment.1 Studies show police AED programs help decrease the time from the 9-1-1 call to first defibrillation, improving overall survival rates2.
SCA is the third leading cause of death in the US3

text_copy_1590852084.text: On average, law enforcement responds to 80 percent of medical emergencies4

text_copy.text: American Heart Association (AHA) recommends a "collapse-to-shock" time of less than three to five minutes5

experiencefragment_c_896937294.text: Hold on to the moments that matter Be ready to act when sudden cardiac arrest strikes Life is built from small moments—coffee before sunrise, sideline cheers, a hand squeezed at the right time. Sudden cardiac arrest can happen to anyone, anywhere, interrupting those moments without warning. Our latest video shows us what’s worth protecting and how being prepared can help. Survivor: Derrick Mosley

After going on a morning run, Derrick began to feel some chest discomfort. His wife, Melissa, a healthcare professional trained in resuscitation, quickly recognized the warning signs of a sudden cardiac arrest. Luckily, an off-duty firefighter pulled over from traffic and began assisting. Soon EMS and Fire/Rescue units arrived to apply a LUCAS.
